module_mood_contract: practitioner fluency — 'I know how to test, I know how to learn, I know how to encode.' Not confidence-as-performance; competence-as-posture.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm this rule prevents: a naming/recognition lecture told before the student has lived the pattern reads as an abstract claim instead of recognition, and steals its own payoff. Not present here — maintainer block: '12–15 min closing lecture for AE101 M6... closes core AE101'; sim trace confirms it fires directly after the spot-gaps-build-the-loop exercise and its Debrief, and the lecture's own opening move ('Look at what you have shipped') only works because the checks it names were just ranked minutes earlier by the student.

Rule binds lectures placed BEFORE a contrast-mood exercise (openers that must not over-teach and collapse the exercise's felt-evidence). This lecture fires AFTER the M6 exercise as its closer (see rule 1 evidence) — the pre-exercise-dosage constraint the rule guards against does not apply to a post-exercise beat.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No cross-module sequencing in lecture bodies.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm this rule prevents: hardcoded module bridges ('M3 reads this file') turn a lecture into a non-reusable, non-relaced piece of shared library. Body carries five M5/M6 refs (lines 7, 9, 20, 26, 32: 'The thing you built at M5', 'M5 used verifier and gate...', 'your verifier from M5, scaled', 'the drift shape you saw at M5', 'the encode loop you ran at M6') — all are recognition of what the SAME module's own exercise just built, not sequencing pointers to a different file. Maintainer block names this explicitly as the check_lectures §3 consolidation carve-out (arc/closer lecture whose SUBJECT is naming what M5-M6 built). Carve-out applies cleanly; harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide/lecture headers pass the squint test AND the truth clause.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Five headers checked: 'Eval' (single-word named-practice takeaway, carve-out applies), 'One primitive, placed wherever there's a bar' (claim the body supports: 'The shape fires on any workflow with a quality bar'), 'The eval primitive scales unchanged' (body: 'The shape doesn't change when the org gets big' — supports 'unchanged' as a claim about shape, not an unsupported universal about outcomes), 'The primitive that runs on cadence' (names the concept), 'Why the loop survives the model' (body argues exactly this via reference/plan/verifier/encode-as-stance-not-tooling). No two slides share a header. No em-dashes, no pedagogy-register headers ('The move', 'The question'). Closest-to-violating candidate is 'scales unchanged' for the universal-word clause, and it stays inside because the body's own claim is scoped to shape, not magnitude.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slide's BODY is size-bounded (~210 readable words AND ≤6 bullets).
rules_evaluated.evidence: Mechanically checked. Command: `node curriculum/evals/scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/lectures/the-loop-has-a-name.md --report` (run from repo root). Output: 'words bul slide header ... 196 3 The primitive that runs on cadence ... 182 3 Why the loop survives the model ... 161 4 Eval ... 119 3 The eval primitive scales unchanged ... 92 2 One primitive, placed wherever there's a bar ... files: 1 slides: 5 limits: 210 words / 6 bullets ... oversized: 0 ... ✓ every slide is within limits'. All five slides under both the word and bullet ceilings.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forcing functions stay, scripted reactions go; forcing functions live in prompts, not body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule binds session exercises with fenced, copy-this prompts that carry the load-bearing move. Grep for fenced code blocks in the file returns zero matches — this is a pure closing lecture with no student action to fence, so there is no forcing function to check for mislocation. Harm (a forcing function accidentally left loose in body prose, skippable by a speed-runner) cannot occur where no forcing function exists.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Classroom = default delivery; body teaches work, trainer manages room outside text.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm this rule prevents: authored conversation cues ('discuss with your neighbor', pause-cues) collapse trainer authority over pacing and read as scripted theatre in a room. Grep of the student-facing body (lines 1-36, above the maintainer fence) for discuss/share/pause/turn-to/talk-to/'the room' returns zero hits — the only 'the room' mentions live in the maintainer's Lecture-meta and Watch-fors notes (lines 47, 110), which are trainer-facing, not student body text. Body stays entirely on the work (naming evals, the Intercom numbers, scheduling primitives, the stance argument).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood contract named / mood-floor 8+ at teaching beats.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm this rule prevents: a teaching beat that reads flat or compliance-shaped when the module's contract demands practitioner fluency. Regenerated Class A trace (whole body = one teaching beat, no setup-only sub-beats) scores mood_score 9 for the phase and close_score 9, is_me_rating 9 — all above the 8+ ship bar, none at the 7 facilitator-premium floor. Trace note: only soft spot is slide 3's Intercom numbers staying one enthusiastic trainer away from vendor-plug feel, which the file's own Watch-fors already flags as a delivery-pacing note, not a text defect.

Harm this rule prevents: an 'unease' or challenge beat reading as 'I messed up' shame instead of 'I'd like to know and can't' not-knowing. This module's mood is fluency, not unease, but the adjacent risk is the model-replacement line (line 31, 'The specific Claude you used today will be replaced') landing as anxiety-inducing rather than epistemic. Trace: persona feels 'a small jolt... followed by relief at The work gets faster. The method does not' — the line resolves into permission, not shame or dread. Watch-fors §5 explicitly directs 'Flat epistemic candour, no sales varnish' for this exact beat, confirming the register is deliberate.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm this rule prevents: titling/heading a teaching beat by the mistake it corrects rather than the practice it builds, which frames the student as already-wrong. All five headers and the title name a positive discipline or artifact ('eval', 'one primitive... placed', 'scales unchanged', 'runs on cadence', 'survives the model') — none lead with a failure word (no 'drift', 'rot', 'blind spot' as a header). The closest failure-adjacent language ('plausible-but-wrong is the default failure mode', line 32) is one clause inside a body sentence building toward the positive discipline (verifier), not a lead.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategy-fidelity — no front-running downstream teaching, module arc respected, Big Idea fidelity, mood resolves without stealing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm this rule prevents: a lecture claiming a teaching moment or resolution that belongs to a different module/lecture, or asserting a Big Idea the strategy doc doesn't license. Checked against `content-strategy-agentic-engineering-101.md` §'M6 in detail': (a) Big Idea fidelity — strategy's scripted framing ('your verifier is an eval; your judge is an eval; your gate is an eval... Practitioners call them judges when LLM-based, verifiers when deterministic, gates when placed in CI') is rendered faithfully in body lines 7-9, with the naming-as-definition-not-survey stance from the backing block's 2026-08-01 decision correctly NOT restored as a claimed convergence; the Ramp anchor case named in strategy is absent from body, but the maintainer block already records this as an intentional, dated decision (orphaned stamp, kept for provenance) — an existing accept-note, not a fresh foul. (b) Scheduled-agents section matches strategy's 'callout, not an exercise' instruction verbatim in shape (three fits named, explicit 'You do not have to wire it today'). (c) Module arc — maintainer block's stated closer chain (loop-has-a-name → the-map-filled-in → agents-that-build-agents) matches the strategy doc's Debrief section, which routes the arc-recognition work to the Human close + 'the-map-filled-in', consistent with this file naming no specific next lecture. (d) Mood resolution — this file resolves its OWN arc (the loop-survives-the-model permission beat) completely (trace close_score 9, is_me 9) while explicitly declining to claim the full M6 close, leaving that to the chain's later files ('Do not restore [a pointer to a named next beat]; the forward-lean... is thematic, not a tee') — earned resolution at this file's own scope, not a stolen or premature resolution of the larger arc.
